delivery_semantics.ordering: no ordering guarantee is claimed across Firehose PutRecordBatch requests; consumers use event_time and transaction_id
delivery_semantics.duplicate_policy: transaction_id is the downstream idempotency key; consumers must tolerate replayed duplicates
delivery_semantics.recovery_point_objective: every Firehose-accepted source event is copied to immutable S3 raw backup; the publisher must report zero failed puts
delivery_semantics.recovery_time_objective: operator-driven replay; target less than 60 minutes after diagnosis, not yet load-tested

required_fields.run_id: non-empty string used for lineage and verification

encryption_boundary.transport: The Firehose Direct PUT delivery stream uses its AWS-owned CMK for the managed transport buffer.
encryption_boundary.durable_data: S3 raw, curated, error, artifact, and evidence objects use the Phase 5 ZIPCO customer-managed KMS key.
encryption_boundary.logs: Lambda and Firehose CloudWatch log groups use the Phase 5 ZIPCO customer-managed KMS key.
encryption_boundary.alerts: The SNS alert topic uses a dedicated rotating customer-managed KMS key whose policy authorizes CloudWatch alarms.

mandatory_controls.assertion: CloudFormation stack status is CREATE_COMPLETE or UPDATE_COMPLETE.
Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream status is ACTIVE.
Firehose uses Direct PUT ingestion.
Firehose transport-buffer encryption is enabled with an AWS-owned CMK.
The Lambda transformer state is Active.
The transformer enforces event schema version 2.1.0.
Firehose dynamic partitioning is enabled.
Firehose backs up all source records to S3.
Firehose Lambda record processing is enabled.
Firehose buffering is bounded between 60 and 900 seconds.
The verification batch is observed in the S3 raw backup.
All expected-valid verification records are observed in curated S3.
Expected-invalid records produce at least one object under the S3 error prefix.
Observed raw, curated, and error objects use SSE-KMS.
The streaming CloudWatch dashboard is retrievable.
Exactly four streaming metric alarms are deployed.
Exactly one composite streaming-health alarm is deployed.
Firehose delivery logging is active with 30-day retention.
The alert SNS topic uses a rotating customer-managed KMS key whose policy permits CloudWatch alarm publication.
The test publisher reports zero Firehose put failures.

failure_injection.method: Publish one missing-key event, one negative-amount event, and one unsupported-schema event.
failure_injection.expected_result: Valid events reach curated S3; invalid events are isolated under the Firehose error prefix; every source record remains in raw backup.

guardrails: The deployment never deletes or rewrites historical source objects.
Replay is a dry run unless --execute is explicitly supplied.
The Lambda function logs aggregate counts only, not transaction payloads.
The optional SNS email subscription remains pending until the recipient confirms it.
This phase does not claim exactly-once processing or a tested disaster-recovery RTO.
